endorsements.name: Danish Tariq
endorsements.label: CVE-2023-6777
endorsements.description: The WP Go Maps (formerly WP Google Maps) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated API key disclosure in versions up to, and including, 9.0.34 due to the plugin adding the API key to several plugin files. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain the developer's Google API key. While this does not affect the security of sites using this plugin, it allows unauthenticated attackers to make requests using this API key with the potential of exhausting requests resulting in an inability to use the map functionality offered by the plugin.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: MEDIUM (CVSS 3.1, 5.3)

povs.explanation: A published CVE record provides public, independently verifiable recognition of the credited vulnerability disclosure.

endorsements.name: Danish Tariq
endorsements.label: Secret Scanning in Open Source at Scale (in-depth)
endorsements.description: We would be demonstrating the numbers and impact to an audience in this talk and we would also be providing ways to prevent this and automation to integrate in your own ci/cd pipelines to prevent such disasters from happening We would be presenting our research done on a large scale after in-house scanning on: This could pose a risk to anyone using those packages as dependencies or plugins so that this chain of not re-inventing the wheel could become a disaster that stops the wheel once and for all. In this in-house research, we have conducted research on publicly available open-source assets like (JS packages), WordPress Plugins, and Ruby Gems to find out the presence of mistakenly or deliberately publicly exposed secrets (including private API keys and so on) i.e. AWS, Google, etc. (33 different types!) Supply chain security conversation is booming these days after attacks like log4j came to the scene.
